hero.sub: Sightline is a teleprompter that follows your voice. It scrolls your script word by word as you speak, pauses when you pause, and keeps the text right beside the camera on iPhone and Mac. No foot pedal, no lost lines.

devices.title: Own the room.
devices.title_accent: Even when it’s a video call.
devices.body: You’re leading a meeting. Presenting a proposal. Explaining a difficult idea. Your notes are ready, but finding them means looking away. On Mac, Sightline sits just below the camera. It stays with you across apps and full-screen spaces, and you can choose to hide it from screen sharing and recordings. The people on the call see you. You see the words you need.
devices.demo_script: Welcome back to the channel. Today I am reading this script straight to the camera. The words keep up with me, so my eyes can stay on the lens.

autosize.title: Find your distance.
autosize.body: Sit close. Lean back. Step away for a wider shot. On iPhone, Sightline estimates your distance using the front camera and gently adjusts the text when you pause. On Mac, choose a reading-distance preset or enable optional camera-based sizing. Your words stay comfortable to read without constant adjustments.
autosize.mac_note: On Mac, you pick how far you sit or let the built-in camera measure it. The camera stays off until you turn it on, and nothing is saved or sent.
autosize.script: Look at the lens, take a breath, and say it the way you would say it to a friend.
autosize.cap_note: From here the text stops growing, so each line still fits on the screen.
autosize.caption: Example sizes for an iPhone 16 Pro.

cases.title: For every time

items.title: Present without searching for your notes.
items.body: Walk through a proposal, lead a team update or teach live. Keep the script near your webcam while you look toward the people on the call. When sharing your screen, choose to hide Sightline from the capture.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a person on a video call on a MacBook with the script panel below the camera notch

items.title: Speak to viewers, not to the scroll.
items.body: Keep your delivery natural even when you pause, take a breath or improvise. Sightline matches the words in your script instead of pushing text past you at a fixed speed.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a creator recording a YouTube intro with Sightline Prompter on iPhone

items.title: Short videos. More eye contact.
items.body: Keep your message close to the lens in portrait or landscape. Frame a wide take with the live 9:16 guide, so you know what will remain in a vertical edit.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: a person filming a short vertical video on iPhone with the script floating over the preview

items.title: Teach the lesson. Keep your flow.
items.body: Follow long explanations without reaching for the screen. Add private delivery cues for emphasis or a pause; Sightline shows the cues without counting them as spoken words.
items.alt: Illustrative scene: an instructor recording an online lesson at a desk with a script on screen

cases.intro: Team updates. Client pitches. Webinars. Online lessons. Interviews. YouTube videos. Short-form content. Sightline isn’t only for making videos. It’s for speaking to people when you want to be prepared without looking distracted.

crop.title: Record the message.
crop.body: On iPhone, Sightline combines your camera preview, script, and recording controls. Choose a compatible microphone. Use live framing guides to plan a vertical crop and keep the shot level. With Pro, record up to 4K at 60 frames per second, HDR, or ProRes on supported devices. Your attention belongs on the message, not on managing the equipment.

languages.title: Your voice.
languages.body: Speak in English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin and more. Sightline supports 31 languages and regional variants; many use on-device recognition when the matching language model is available.
languages.note: The free version follows your voice in English, Turkish and Spanish. Sightline Pro adds the rest. Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese are matched in segments, so accuracy is lower than in languages written with spaces.

library.title: Write once.
library.body: Draft or import a script on Mac. Pick it up on iPhone through your iCloud library. Bring in Word documents, PDFs, Markdown, and more. Add delivery cues for a pause, a smile, or a change of emphasis. Sightline shows them to you without treating them as words to speak. One preparation. More ways to deliver it.
library.cue_note: Cues in double brackets show on screen as small reminders. They are never read aloud and never counted as words.
library.formats_label: Import: Word, PDF, Markdown, RTF, HTML, OpenDocument, text

pro.note: Try voice following for up to two minutes per run in English, Turkish, or Spanish. On iPhone, record short videos in 1080p for free. Go Pro for longer sessions, advanced video recording, pace information, and 31 supported languages and regional variants. Choose a monthly, yearly, or one-time purchase. One Pro purchase covers both iPhone and Mac.

items.q: Can I use Sightline during video calls without showing my notes?
items.a: Yes. On Mac, the prompter stays near the camera above your other apps, including full-screen spaces. You can set its window to stay out of screen sharing and recordings, so you see your notes without putting them into the shared image.

items.q: How does a teleprompter that follows your voice work?
items.a: It listens while you read and matches what it hears to the words on screen. The text moves when you speak and waits when you pause, so you set the pace. It only matches words that are in your script, so a cough, an ad-lib or a skipped line does not make it jump.

items.q: Is there a free teleprompter app that follows your voice?
items.a: Yes. The free version follows your voice for up to 2 minutes per run in English, Turkish and Spanish, and records up to 2 minutes of 1080p video on iPhone. Sightline Pro removes the limits.

Many languages are recognized on the device and work without a connection. If a language has no offline model installed, the audio goes to Apple's speech service, and the app tells you on screen. For Turkish, on-device recognition needs the iOS Dictation model.

31 languages and regional variants, including English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Cantonese and Turkish. The free version covers English, Turkish and Spanish. Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese are matched in segments, so accuracy is lower than in languages written with spaces.

items.q: What if I go off script?
items.a: The text stays where you are. A cough, an ad-lib or a skipped line does not make it jump. It moves only when you say words that are on screen.

items.q: Do I need a MacBook with a notch?
items.a: No. On a MacBook with a notch, the panel sits right below it. On a Mac without one, the panel sits at the top center of the screen.

items.q: How does auto text size work?
items.a: On iPhone, the front camera estimates how far your face is from the screen and sizes the text to match, so the letters stay comfortable to read at that distance. It also limits line length and the number of lines, so your eyes stay near the lens. On Mac, you pick a distance preset or turn on the optional camera measurement. Measuring happens on your device, and no video or face data leaves it.

Yes, on iPhone. The app records with the script floating over the live preview and saves the video to your Photos library. The Mac app is a prompter panel for calls and recordings you make with other tools.

items.q: Does one purchase cover iPhone and Mac?
items.a: Yes. It is one app on the App Store, and Sightline Pro unlocks both the iPhone and the Mac version. Both use the same iCloud script library.
Sightline Pro is available as a subscription with a free trial, or as a one-time purchase. The App Store shows current prices in your local currency.
Plain text, Markdown, Word, PDF, RTF, HTML and OpenDocument files. Scripts sync between iPhone and Mac through iCloud.

items.q: Can I use a game controller?
items.a: Yes. A DualSense controller works with the Mac app over Bluetooth or USB. The analog stick scrolls, and buttons change speed and jump between paragraphs. Controller support is part of Sightline Pro.

Your scripts stay in your own iCloud Drive. There are no ads and no tracking across apps, and you do not need a Sightline account. Sync uses your iCloud account, so you need to be signed in to iCloud on the device. Anonymous usage counts can be switched off in Settings.

close.title: Look up. Keep your place.
close.sub: And now, the only thing left is to speak.

pace.title: Your pace.
pace.body: Pause to think. Emphasize a point. Say something that wasn’t in your notes. Sightline matches your speech to the words in your script. It waits when you pause and holds your place when you improvise. No scrolling speed to chase. No rushing through a sentence just because the text keeps moving.

connection.title: Less reading.
connection.body: On iPhone, a short band of text stays near the front camera. On Mac, your words sit close to the webcam. You can follow a script while keeping your gaze closer to the people listening. Prepared doesn’t have to look rehearsed.

privacy.title: Your scripts.
privacy.body: Your scripts live in your own iCloud Drive. There’s no separate Sightline account, no ads, and no tracking across apps. Many languages can use on-device speech recognition when the appropriate model is available.
